findings.evidence: getZestIconElement checks `name in ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS` (line 167), so inherited Object.prototype keys pass as known icons. A probe rendering <ZestIcon name="__proto__" /> threw "Objects are not valid as a React child (found: object with keys {})" under React 18; name="toString" returned Object.prototype.toString and rendered an empty <span class="zestIcon"> instead of null.
findings.description: R5 requires an unknown icon name to render nothing and not throw, but names that collide with Object.prototype (__proto__, constructor, toString, valueOf, hasOwnProperty) are treated as built-in icons. A library consumer that passes an untrusted string as ZestIcon name (for example a route parameter or API value) can crash the app's render tree (availability/DoS) or render a bogus empty icon. Use a null-prototype map, a Map, or Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(ZEST_ICON_ELEMENTS, name) before indexing.
